review.summary: Accept with corrections. Every frozen verdict was recomputed from the raw logs with my own script (1098 values, 0 mismatches; RESULTS*.json and the report regenerate byte-identically): V19 stage a KILL (C8 at 0.863/0.887 of A1), V21 a1 PASS-I 0.2483/0.2506 and PASS-C 0.578/0.568, a2 PASS-I 0.220/0.221/0.163 with cycles NOT_DECIDABLE, stage b PASS 0.4486/0.4515. Re-runs agree: five validity suites byte for byte, hashes and counts on three wide-band problems for indexed, slices and tight, TA/A0 instructions 0.24828. No commit-order violation. TA and the client follow the protected arithmetic: my fuzz (38,564 matrices) and 40 driver cases found no difference. Corrections: (1) 'the A3 hypothesis is refuted, the kernels are instruction-bound' is contradicted by the authoritative cells: arm B, with the instruction count of the protected kernel, needs 0.565/0.576 of the cycles of A1; (2) REPORT section 2 shows only the busy-host measurement, not the deciding one, and calls the partition arms slower although they are faster there; (3) labels: undeclared arm BD, typed-in numbers, 'whole-run' for a 40-attempt prefix (my whole runs: 0.447-0.453).

findings.claim: REPORT_KO.md section 2 (interpretation), the results row of V19 in PREREGISTRATION.md, the last sentence of ledger row L-0320 and the reason of addendum A4 state that the hypothesis of addendum A3 (dependent chain) is refuted and that the banded kernels are bound by the instruction count.
findings.evidence: Deciding cells logs/measure_m2_n10000.jsonl and logs/measure_m3_n100000.jsonl (load 1.9-3.1): arm B, the reordered back substitution of A3, executes 163.0/163.7 instructions per row and solve (A0 162.0/162.7, A1 152.0/152.8) in 32.6/33.3 cycles per row against 60.3/61.1 (A0) and 65.5/66.3 (A1); per stage pattern B needs 0.565/0.576 of A1 and 0.600/0.609 of A0 (spreads 0.017/0.079). Exploratory arms: BD (division kept, valid under V2 and V3) 0.612 of A1 at n=1e4, B3 0.501/0.509 of A0. V21 cells: at 42 instructions per row and solve TA needs 35.5/36.1, TD 26.5/27.2, TS 15.0/15.4 cycles per row; TD (valid) is at 0.449/0.444 of A0 and 0.417/0.415 of A1, inside the numerical pass levels of V19. A1 has 0.918 of the instructions of A0 and 1.06-1.08 of its cycles. My diagnostic runs: B/A1 0.62 (1e4) and 0.57 (1e5).
findings.correction: Keep the frozen verdict KILL (the only valid declared arms are C8 and CV8). Replace the interpretation: KILL follows from the validity rule (B misses V2 with 1.7e-14 against 1e-14); the dependent chain is a real cost, reordering alone halves the solve cycles at unchanged instruction count, and with a valid sequential arm the outcome would have been FAIL. Instruction count and chain are two levers of similar size on the solves. Supersede the last sentence of L-0320 and add a dated note to the results section and PROGRESS.md.

findings.claim: REPORT_KO.md section 2 documents the V19 verdict KILL with tables of cycle ratios and says the partition arms are slower.
findings.evidence: build_report.py:36-38 and 137-138 print only the first complete measurement of each size (logs/measure_m1_*.jsonl, load 38->27.9 and 27.9->14.5, spreads up to 1.09, 'load rule met: False'). The files that decide the verdict (verdicts.per_size in RESULTS.json: logs/measure_m2_n10000.jsonl, logs/measure_m3_n100000.jsonl) are not rendered; 0.863 and 0.887 appear nowhere in the report, which shows C8 at 1.246/1.744 of A1 and B at 0.702/0.764. On the deciding cells C2, C4 and C8 need 0.85-0.89 of the cycles of A1 and 0.90-0.94 of A0, so the sentence that the partition arms are slower is false there (only the CV arms are slower: 1.17-1.25 of A1).
findings.correction: Render the measurement named in verdicts.per_size for each size (all measurements if space allows) and correct the sentence about the partition arms.

findings.claim: Addendum A4: thresholds were fixed before any timing run or instruction count of TA, TD or the whole-run mode existed; the reason cites the first rounds of the running V19 measurement.
findings.evidence: File evidence supports the first part: second binary built 14:48:50 (sha256 54f4bc07, as PREDECLARED_V21.json), xcheck logs 14:49:19, commit 9ad4282f 14:52:41, first drive_v run started 14:52:59, first measure_v run 15:00:54; no measure_x or drive_x file exists. Sibling arms were at 0.90-0.97 of the instructions of A0, so 0.40 was not fitted (measured 0.25); the cycle margin is thin (0.578/0.568 against 0.60). Order notes: 1ac99cf7 (TA, TD, TS code and validity logs, then labelled exploratory) precedes 9ad4282f, as A4 declares; 7d78de29 (PREDECLARED_V21B.json) follows 750b8e42 (drive_v1 logs) and the start of measure_v1, the stage b thresholds being frozen earlier in 9ad4282f. The output of the smoke run named in A4 was not kept. Not verifiable by me: pushes to the remote and the absence of unlogged ad-hoc runs.

findings.claim: REPORT section 3 and the results section leave a switch of the facade's kernel to Slices to the owner.
findings.evidence: The narrow control of stage a2 (logs/drive_v2_bruss1d5000.jsonl, authoritative) shows Slices at 0.980 of the instructions but 1.143 of the cycles of Indexed on band 2; this is in the table and not in the text or the results row. The protected file also holds BandedKernel::FixedWidth2 (rodas5p_fast.rs:195-197, 560-641), which A4 and the report do not mention: my runs give 0.915 of the instructions of Indexed and 1.05-1.13 of its cycles (diagnostic).
findings.correction: Add to the owner note: Slices gains on wide bands (0.40 of the cycles, authoritative on two of three problems) and costs about 14% on band 2, so a kernel switch should depend on the band width; the new client needs about 0.49 of the instructions of FixedWidth2.

findings.claim: banded_tight.rs: nothing allocates after new; the client behaves as BandedStageLu.
findings.evidence: Read side by side with BandState::factor and solve (rodas5p_fast.rs:375-437, 528-558) I found no arithmetic difference: assembly (-J) + inv on all slots, strict-greater pivot search, swap of columns k..k+4, skip on a multiplier equal to 0.0 (also -0.0), ascending row updates, substitutions in the protected order, last four columns and rows through the general step. Counters and the singular-pivot error text are equal (checked at every column). Differences outside the driver's call sequence: solve_fixed2 computes p - k (lines 269, 282), which underflows if solve_in_place is called before a successful factor (pivots are zero): panic in a debug build, wrap in release, where BandedStageLu never panics. The singular-pivot path allocates the error message, as the protected kernel does. The node's tests have a singular pivot at column 0 only, no non-autonomous problem and the allocation test at n = 1000 only; my tests cover zero columns and NaN or infinite entries at every position, interchanges in the last columns, ties, denormals, n = 3 to 1000, non-finite shifts, a non-autonomous problem, rejected steps, attempt budgets and an injected non-finite Jacobian entry.
findings.correction: Optional: document the precondition or use a wrapping subtraction, adjust the sentence on allocation, add a test with a singular pivot in the last four columns.

findings.claim: The measurement program and the parsers guard the timed runs.
findings.evidence: runner/src/main.rs:481-483: the checksum is an XOR over an even number of identical patterns, so every BENCH line prints checksum=0000000000000000 and does not witness the solution of the timed run (validity rests on the check mode). build_results_v21.py:63-65 and 118 skip failed runs silently, build_results.py:140 skips incomplete rounds, and no parser caps the measurement index at three.
